So even an owner given read tools would have found nothing addressed to it","source":"art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29 (item I28)","statement":"RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-29, item I28 of art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29.

① OBSERVED. The owner agent refused to ratify "18 components" from a one-line summary: "I won't ratify a parts list I haven't seen." It needed a second round to be sent each name with its job. Its only read of anything in a design was exported JSON on disk (flo2's and reflow2's own exports, used to catch a 2× sizing error). It never read the design it was deciding for. Expected: an owner can see, in plain language, what it is being asked to approve, with the evidence. NOT affected: the designer, who read everything through the tools.

② PRECEDENT.
- req:the-loop-says-what-is-owed-to-a-person (proposed): loop_status(contributor_id) → assigned_decisions plus gaps on owned ground.
- req:the-agent-renders-the-design-for-the-reader-who-needs-it (accepted): the agent renders a view for a reader it is TALKING to.
- flo2: dec:idea-your-flo2-account-page-shows-your-designs and dec:idea-ruling-on-a-decision-from-the-browser (both open).

③ CANDIDATES.
(a) SETUP: the hub withheld the owner's design tools on purpose, to keep it independent.
(b) The per-person read exists but cannot address THIS owner.
(c) Questions, which are what the owner answered, have no addressee.
(d) The observation is wrong: the summaries were enough and the owner was being fussy.

④⑤ MEASURED 2026-09-29.
· (a) HOLDS in part: the owner had no design tools by the hub's choice.
· (b) CONFIRMED by reading the contract. loop_status's served description says "Only ASSIGNMENT is attributed: an `AUTHORED_BY role=approver` edge". flo2's bindApprovals refuses any approver but the signed-in account (measured in-process today). So nothing in 50f966697d6c5024 could be assigned to who:owner, and loop_status(contributor_id: who:owner) would list nothing.
· (c) CONFIRMED: Question has no addressee field (see fact:root-cause-answering-takes-two-calls-and-records-no-answerer-because-the-answers-edge-landed-as-its-own-tool-2026-09-29).
· (d) REFUTED by outcome: when shown the parts list, the owner amended part 5 (operator fields and two clocks on every fact), which the summary had hidden.

⑥ CLASS: every read the loop serves assumes the reader is the agent's own user, in the session. A second party who must JUDGE (a delegated owner, a reviewer, a manager) has no addressed view. The same shape as the Question model in I29, and the hub trial's "end the human middleman" goal cannot be met without it. Giving the owner tools alone would not fix it: (b) and (c) mean there is nothing addressed to it to read.

⑦⑧ OWED. No test and no fix. The companion ideas (an owner-scoped digest, a question batch as a record) are brainstorms.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED. Whether a human owner using flo2's browser would be better served. flo2 renders no decisions or questions for a person today (both ideas are open), so probably not.","subject_id":"req:the-loop-says-what-is-owed-to-a-person","valid_from":"2026-09-29"}
